summary:
We developed HELIOS (High-Elevation Lunar Illumination & Orbital Site Advisor), an interactive mission-planning web platform for NASA’s Artemis III Lunar South Pole campaign. Selecting a lunar south-pole landing site requires balancing competing constraints: grazing solar illumination for power, direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight for communications, safe touchdown slopes, and proximity to Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) containing water ice.

HELIOS unifies real NASA ephemeris and topography into one workspace: a 3D Sun–Earth–Moon orbital and south-polar terrain explorer, a multi-site illumination and communications timeline analyzer, a side-by-side mission scenario comparison tool, and an AI mission advisor powered by Google Gemini with a deterministic NASA-grounded scoring engine. Rather than fabricating metrics, HELIOS evaluates all 9 official Artemis III candidate regions (plus historic Apollo 11–17 sites for context) using authentic NASA JPL Horizons, LRO LOLA DEM, and NASA Moon Trek datasets to support transparent, evidence-based landing decisions.
details:
HELIOS is a full-stack lunar mission intelligence platform built around four connected modules:

  1. 3D Lunar Environment & Topography Explorer: Interactive Three.js orbital simulation of the Sun, Earth, and Moon paired with NASA Moon Trek south-polar imagery and LRO LOLA elevation data, allowing users to inspect the 9 Artemis III candidate regions (and compare them with historic Apollo 11–17 landing sites) and replay local horizon/terrain obstruction.
  2. Power & Communications Analyzer: Computes geometric solar illumination availability and direct-to-Earth line-of-sight windows over user-defined UTC mission durations (1 to 720 hours) using NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris (coord@301).
  3. Scenario Comparison Workspace: Side-by-side comparison of candidate sites across sunlight %, Earth visibility %, LOLA mean/max slope, RMS surface roughness, elevation, safety rating, and distance to the nearest PSR.
  4. HELIOS AI Mission Advisor: A multi-turn conversational assistant that accepts natural-language mission descriptions or general lunar questions. It extracts structured mission parameters, runs deterministic constraint filtering and weighted suitability scoring across all 9 Artemis III regions, and uses Google Gemini (with a deterministic local fallback) to explain trade-offs, disqualifications, and scientific rationale without inventing unmeasured data.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
HELIOS makes complex orbital geometry, solar illumination trade-offs, and south-polar terrain safety accessible in a single transparent tool—helping mission planners, researchers, and students understand why specific Artemis III regions succeed or fail under different mission durations and power/communication constraints.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, OpenLayers (ol), Recharts, Lucide React
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, httpx, NumPy, Pandas, Uvicorn
  • AI & Data Integration: Google Gemini API (gemini-2.5-flash / gemini-2.0-flash / gemini-flash-lite-latest), NASA JPL Horizons REST API, local ephemeris & LOLA DEM JSON caching

Creativity & Factors Considered:

  • Scientific Integrity: Missing measurements are never replaced with zeros, and geometric line-of-sight is explicitly distinguished from RF link quality or electrical power output.
  • Immersive Space-Grade UX: Full-screen historic NASA lunar EVA video hero with scroll-driven fade into an animated cosmic backdrop, translucent telemetry cards, and an interactive 3D lunar globe.
